A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, and Appendices A-D are readable and support reliable matching across the restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 Sections 7.1-7.2, Figure 6, and Appendix D report original experiments on polynomial expressivity and attainable classification accuracy using synthetic data.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments in Sections 6.1-6.2, Figure 5, and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The underlying strategic-response model and experimental procedures are retained. Appendix C.10 discusses prospective inversion and curvature-regularization approaches without introducing an instantiated learning algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same bounded two-dimensional polynomial classifiers and synthetic class-conditional Gaussian classification problems. The additional discussion of other cost functions introduces no evaluated datasets or scenarios.

E2.justification: The approximation experiment retains the same comparators: unrestricted non-strategic classification and optimal linear classification, whose strategic and non-strategic classes coincide. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Appendix D retains the polynomial-degree and strategic-reach ranges, bounded input domain, 0.9 fitting tolerance, Gaussian-separation range, and 25 samples per class. The grid-based calculations and optimal-linear-classifier search are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The same experiments examine expressivity across polynomial degree and strategic reach, and accuracy across class separation and strategic reach. No empirical ablation, robustness test, or supplementary case study is added; the new appendix analyses concern theory and its implications.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 instances for expressivity and 20 for approximation, with means and standard-error confidence intervals. No repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: The experimental plots in v1 Figure 6 and v2 Figure 5 are identical, and their reported trends and comparator relationships are retained. The revised mathematical examples preserve their intended findings and are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 3 and Appendix B.10, bounding strategic VC dimension for piecewise-linear classes by O(dm log m + nu_p k log k); the original polytope bound remains as Theorem 4. It also revises the classifier construction in Appendix B.8 and replaces the flawed strategic-accuracy example in v1 C.8 with a corrected construction in v2 C.9. Equation (1) corrects the response objective from h(x) to h(x').

C1.justification: The introduction adds a central contribution establishing an upper bound on strategic complexity for bounded piecewise-linear classes, including fixed-size ReLU networks. This substantially extends v1's polytope-specific upper-bound claim, while retaining the claims about complexity collapse, non-universality, and approximation gaps.

C2.justification: New Appendices A.2-A.3, C.1, and C.10 substantially expand applicability and interpretation: bounded input domains, obstacles to a general VC bound, extensions beyond Euclidean costs, and limitations under instance-dependent costs. They also develop implications for inversion, curvature regularization, interpolation thresholds, and model selection.

D1.justification: v2 Section 6 adds a code-repository link for both experiments. Appendix D.1 further clarifies the existing grid approximation; the disclosed CPU allocation, sample counts, fitting procedure, and tolerance remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Huang (2020) and Petersen and Voigtlaender (2018) to connect piecewise-linear analysis with ReLU approximation. It also clarifies the borrowing from offset-curve theory and discusses restrictions of earlier optimization approaches, while retaining the existing related-work framework.

P1.justification: v2 combines 'Points' and 'Classifiers' under 'Underlying Mechanisms,' renames 'Model classes' to 'Class-level analysis,' and adds appendix subsections and acknowledgments. Copyediting and notation cleanup are widespread, but the original bottom-up sequence and most existing exposition remain.

P2.justification: Both versions retain eleven figures and no tables. v2 revises point-mapping arrows and explanatory captions, moves the curvature illustration from the main text to Appendix B.3, and relocates the unchanged experimental figure nearer the experiment descriptions.

improvement.justification: The new piecewise-linear VC bound and accompanying proof substantially broaden the central learnability analysis beyond v1's polytope result to classes relevant to ReLU networks. Corrected mathematical constructions, explicit applicability boundaries, and code-access information further improve reliability and usefulness. The fully general learnability question remains open, and the empirical evidence is unchanged.
